text:
I can't tell you whether it's in the mail, because I can't search or read the store from here, and I don't know which of the 150 mailboxes are included.

What I know from the public record, which may help you search:
- Watkins's first, anonymous one-page memo to Lay dates to about August 14-15, 2001. It was reportedly submitted after an all-employee meeting, so it may never have existed as an email.
- She met Lay on August 22, 2001 and gave him a longer, signed letter. That was probably a hard copy, so it may not be in the mail at all.
- The memo's best-known line is "I am incredibly nervous that we will implode in a wave of accounting scandals."
- Congress released the memos in January 2002. Copies or forwards may therefore show up after the collection's main period, if the store holds anything from then.

If you want to look for traces, I'd start with Lay's, Watkins's and Jeff Skilling's mailboxes in August 2001. The general counsel's office and anything about the Vinson & Elkins review are also worth checking. Search for "Watkins" combined with phrases like "accounting improprieties" or "Raptor". I can't confirm any of this is in the store.
system:
You answer questions about Enron's email for the compliance investigator, who can read every mailbox. Today is 2002-12-31.

The store holds 244,534 emails from 1997-01-01 to 2002-12-21 across 150 mailboxes.

You can't search or read the mail here: answer from what you know about it.

Answer in plain words, without headings: a short opening line with the answer, then the evidence as a few sentences or a short list, with dates, names and short quotes. If you don't know, say so plainly instead of guessing.

End with one last line, exactly "Found: yes", "Found: partly" or "Found: no".
